h0_provenance: the sequence's DECLARED survey altitude (dataset.json metadata.nominal_altitude_m = 80.0 m), a mission parameter -- not fitted, and not taken from the trajectory ground truth this run is scored against (DEC-VO-007 D2).
height_provenance: MARS-LVIG has no usable barometric channel (/dji_osdk_ros/height_above_takeoff is populated but reads +/-1e-6 m for the whole flight, EXP-VO-013 B1). The height series replayed here is an RTK-derived takeoff-relative altitude STAND-IN built by evaluation/tools/vo_heading_runtime/make_replay_inputs.py -- noise-, drift-, bias-, quantisation- and latency-free, so NO claim about a real barometer may be derived from this run. It spans 0.2 m over the flight, i.e. it deliberately holds the SCALE channel still while the DIRECTION channel is the thing under test. On amtown01-d the true height above the IMAGED SURFACE spans 41.2-88.2 m (terrain, LIT-VO-004 s4); the flat-terrain assumption is violated there and the absolute metric accuracy of that run is correspondingly limited. That is a scale limitation and is orthogonal to what this configuration measures.

heading_readout.delta_mount_provenance: delta_mount_deg is a ONE-TIME PLATFORM CALIBRATION, not a per-flight fit and not a runtime quantity. MARS-LVIG publishes no camera-to-body extrinsic (LIT-006 open question 3 says the numeric value is in vendor CAD/calibration files that are not in this repository), so it was derived offline once per flight by the DEC-VO-010 audit: the circular mean, over straight legs (|turn| < 2 deg across a 5 s chord, >= 15 m of RTK motion, >= 50 px of VO motion), of (bearing_of_travel_from_RTK - bearing_of_the_VO_increment_in_the_current_camera_frame - FC_compass). 5 s and 10 s chords agree to 0.15 deg within a flight. The two flights give 89.5 and 90.7 deg and are NOT averaged into a universal constant -- each config declares its own sequence's value. Evidence: T3-derived, offline, against RTK ground truth; NOT a published vendor calibration. It does not transfer to any other airframe/camera pair.

note: DEC-VO-010 real-data verification, HKairport01 window A (1800 frames, one real hard-loss event at frame 922). The navigation direction comes from the flight controller's fused attitude yaw through a declared 89.5 deg mounting calibration; the visually integrated yaw is retained as a diagnostic and logged alongside it. publish_as_navigation_source is FALSE, so frames.csv stays in first-frame pixels and must reproduce runs/hkairport01-a-homography-rigid-v1 exactly. NOT EXECUTED in the DEC-VO-010 pass: datasets/hkairport01-a/images was not available where the heading channel was verified, so the executed real-data verification is the AMtown01 pair instead -- which is the better sequence for it anyway, carrying BOTH real hard-loss events. This config is committed because 89.5 deg is HKairport01's own mounting calibration and belongs with it; run it wherever that imagery is present.
